rulings.challenge_claim: The person-shift ground offered for the Isa.45.1 seam is byte-false at the cited verse: 45:1 speaks of Cyrus in the third person exactly as the preceding verse does, and direct second-person address begins only at 45:2.
rulings.grounds: The byte-false half is confirmed; the 'exactly as the preceding verse does' half is not, and the severity comes down with it. CONFIRMED: MT 45:1 carries no second-person form anywhere -- the body runs אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱזַ֣קְתִּי בִֽימִינ֗וֹ and לְרַד לְפָנָיו֙ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.1), a first-person perfect governing a third-person suffix and 'before him' twice -- while direct address opens at אֲנִי֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֵלֵ֔ךְ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.2) and runs on through MT 45:3-45:5; the English witness sets the same distribution at web:Isa.45.1 against web:Isa.45.2. So the row's 'now addressed directly in second person' is byte-false at the verse it cites and must be re-anchored at MT 45:2 or dropped. NOT CONFIRMED: MT 45:1 is not the same construction as MT 44:28. MT 45:1 is a fresh verse-initial messenger formula naming its own ADDRESSEE, כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִמְשִׁיחוֹ֮ לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.1), whereas MT 44:28 is הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.28), a participle inside the participle chain of the frame that opened at MT 44:24. That addressee-naming is itself byte-visible and tier-1, and it is the ground the row states FIRST and states correctly, so the seam does not depend on the defective clause -- which puts the challenge one severity band high. The remaining objects verify: the frame is verse-initial with the tetragrammaton adjacent; the mark set is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH after MT 45:7 and MT 45:8 inside the span, SAMEKH after MT 44:28 cited before it, tier-3, single-witness); and the ketiv/qere at MT 45:2 is real, staged as an unpointed ketiv beside its pointed qere, with no splice crossing it. NEW FINDING, neither primary's: the row's 'Israel/Jacob again NAMED as servant' at MT 45:4 repeats a byte-imprecision already standing in this part at MT 44:1 -- עַבְדִּ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּחִירִ֑י (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.4) names Jacob servant and Israel CHOSEN, the same construction as the earlier verse -- so the cure is a two-row sweep, not a spot fix; the referent is correctly left undecided in both.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-012. (a) Field boundary_rationale: delete 'now addressed directly in second person' from the MT 45:1 clause. Either re-anchor the person claim at MT 45:2 -- splicing אֲנִי֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֵלֵ֔ךְ at byte tier and adding oshb:Isa.45.2 to boundary_evidence_refs -- or drop it and let the seam rest on what is byte-true at MT 45:1: a fresh verse-initial messenger formula naming Cyrus as the addressee of the speech, distinct from the participle standing inside the preceding frame's chain at MT 44:28. (b) Field boundary_rationale: correct 'Israel/Jacob again NAMED as servant' to the bytes -- Jacob named servant, Israel named chosen -- keeping the referent undecided, and apply this as a SWEEP across every row in the part carrying that wording rather than a spot fix. Test the cure must pass: every person or form label in the row re-derives from the pointed bytes at the ref it is attached to -- the test that killed the original was that MT 45:1 carries no second-person form at all -- and the servant wording re-checks against the naming construction at each cited verse.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 'direct rhetorical question' that carries this row's form label is not in the Hebrew of Isa.45.11: the verse holds no interrogative particle at all, and the interrogatives it is said to answer sit in the two preceding woe verses.
rulings.grounds: Byte-exact. MT 45:11 reads הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת שְׁאָל֔וּנִי (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.11) with the he pointed qamets -- the definite article -- against the interrogative he pointed hataf-patah at הֲיֹאמַ֨ר חֹ֤מֶר לְיֹֽצְרוֹ֙ מַֽה תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.9) and at the same particle in MT 45:21; the verse carries no interrogative particle and no interrogative pronoun anywhere, its second verb being תְּצַוֻּֽנִי (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.11), a prefix-conjugation form with the same first-person object suffix. The genuine interrogatives sit in the woe pair the row says it answers -- MT 45:9 and מַה תּוֹלִ֑יד (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.10). Even the rendering does not carry the label: the English the row quotes closes on an exclamation, not a question (web:Isa.45.11). This is heavier than a wording slip because device_notes grounds the declared category on 'its opening rhetorical-challenge form', so the unit_type rests on a construal the bytes do not carry. The category itself survives on a different byte-true ground -- the summons-plus-command shape addressed to a plural, which is what the closed vocabulary asks for in these chapters -- so no unit_type change is warranted and medium is the right band. ONE CORRECTION the remedy must not inherit: the closing formula at MT 45:13 is אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.13) and belongs to the amar-plus-tetragrammaton adjacency object, NOT to the postpositive utterance object the challenge names -- that object stands in 23 verses book-wide and in 0 verses of ch 45, and the two are never blended; the hosts title here is the only such site in ch 45 (sweep: 60 verses book-wide carry the hosts title). The title claim verifies as stated: the plene title spelling stands in 24 verses book-wide with the defective spelling adding a 25th, and MT 45:11 is the only title site inside MT 44:23-45:25. Marks verify: PE after MT 45:13 inside the span, SAMEKH after MT 45:10 cited before it (tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-014. (a) Field boundary_rationale: replace 'a direct rhetorical question' with the byte-visible shape -- the article-marked object followed by a summons form carrying a first-person object suffix and a prefix-conjugation form carrying the same suffix, spliced at byte tier at oshb:Isa.45.11 as הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת שְׁאָל֔וּנִי and תְּצַוֻּֽנִי -- and state expressly that no interrogative particle or pronoun stands in the verse. (b) Field device_notes: re-ground the trial_speech choice on that summons-and-command shape rather than on a question form, and hold the imperative-versus-indicative reading of the first form open, no morphology layer being staged; unit_type, confidence and the disclosed salvation-oracle rival all stand unchanged. (c) Optional rear-seam corroboration: cite the closing speech attribution at MT 45:13 under the CORRECT object -- amar plus the tetragrammaton with the hosts title -- never under the postpositive utterance object, which does not occur in the chapter. Test the cure must pass: every form-class and question label re-derives from the pointed bytes at its cited ref, and every count-object named is the one actually swept -- the test that killed the original was the article-pointed he at MT 45:11 against the interrogative he at MT 45:9.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF (low): the row's label of Isa.45.14 as the 'third koh-amar frame' undercounts the divine speech-formula sequence within this span -- five onsets stand at Isa.44.24, 45:1, 45:11, 45:14 and 45:18, so Isa.45.14 is the fourth, and the undercount silently omits Isa.45.11. OL (medium): the stated ground that 'no addressee shift' marks 45:15 is contradicted by the pointed bytes, which shift from a feminine-singular addressee in 45:14 to a masculine-singular addressee in 45:15; and the row's koh-amar ordinal counts an enumeration it never names.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: the ordinal is the SAME defect in both packets, OL's framing the more complete since it adds the missing count-domain declaration; the addressee item is DISTINCT to OL and is the heavier of the two. Both verify. ORDINAL: the messenger formula stands in exactly 5 verses inside MT 44:23-45:25 -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ at MT 44:24, כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִמְשִׁיחוֹ֮ לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ at MT 45:1, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיֹצְר֑וֹ at MT 45:11, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה at MT 45:14 and כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה at MT 45:18 (byte tier at each ref; sweep: 48 verses book-wide carry the formula) -- so MT 45:14 is the FOURTH onset, and the row reaches 'third' only by skipping the MT 45:11 frame that the neighbouring row itself treats as fresh. OL's added half is the sharper statement of the rule: the ordinal names no counted domain, and the domain cannot be inferred, because a ch-45-only count WOULD yield third while the sibling row numbers MT 45:1 'second' on a count that includes MT 44:24 -- semantic-class count discipline requires the object and the range be named before the digit. ADDRESSEE: byte-contradicted. Every addressee form in MT 45:14 is feminine singular -- עָלַ֤יִךְ יַעֲבֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלָ֣ךְ יִֽהְי֔וּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.14) -- and the confession itself reads אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל (byte tier, same ref), the preposition carrying a final kaf with NO mappiq, i.e. feminine singular; MT 45:15 then opens אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.15) with a masculine singular independent pronoun. The shift is byte-visible whichever speaker is assigned to the confession, since the addressee changes from the city to the deity inside the reported speech itself. The row may still keep MT 45:15 inside the confession, but it must argue that from the reported-speech frame: arguing from the absence of a tier-1 signal is legitimate only when the absence is real, and here it is not. Credit, so the author does not disturb it: the paseq disclosure is exemplary -- count-only, single-witness, position expressly not claimed -- and MT 45:14 is verified as the ONLY paseq-bearing verse in MT 44:23-45:25; the parashah disclosure is symmetric and correctly typed (PE after MT 45:13 before the span, PE after MT 45:17 at its close, tier-3, single-witness). Severity is OL's medium rather than LF's low: the ordinal alone would be low, but the byte-false absence is the stated ground of the row's own internal decision.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-015. (a) Field device_notes: replace the clause grounding the decision on no addressee shift at MT 45:15 with the byte-true argument -- the addressee turns from feminine singular at MT 45:14, עָלַ֤יִךְ יַעֲבֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלָ֣ךְ יִֽהְי֔וּ and אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל, to masculine singular at MT 45:15, אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר, each spliced at byte tier at its own ref, and MT 45:15 is nonetheless held inside the unit as the CONTINUATION OF THE REPORTED CONFESSION, which is the reported-speech frame doing the work; the honest absence to cite there is that no fresh messenger frame opens at MT 45:15. (b) Field boundary_rationale: either name the ordinal's counted object and range explicitly (messenger-formula onsets within MT 44:23-45:25, MT 45:14 being the fourth of five) or drop the ordinal and call it a fresh frame. The same edit is owed in the sibling row that numbers MT 45:18, so run it as ONE series-wide sweep across the part, not as separate spot fixes. Test the cure must pass: any ordinal in row prose names its counted object and range and re-derives against a sweep of that range -- the test that killed the original was the five-onset count in MT 44:23-45:25 -- and any claim that a signal is absent re-checks against the pointed bytes on both sides of the seam it argues.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF (low): the row's label of Isa.45.18 as the 'fourth koh-amar frame' undercounts the same sequence -- by the five-onset count it is the fifth, the undercount again omitting Isa.45.11. OL (medium): the addressee contrast offered as this row's seam driver is half absent from the bytes -- Isa.45.18-Isa.45.19 carry no vocative and no second-person addressee at all, so there is no 'address to the offspring of Jacob' for 45:20's summons to shift away from -- plus the same unnamed-enumeration ordinal.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: the ordinal is the SAME defect in both packets AND the same series defect already ruled on the sibling row -- one cure, not three. The addressee-contrast item is DISTINCT to OL and is the substantive finding here. Both verify. ORDINAL: by the verified five-onset count inside MT 44:23-45:25, MT 45:18 is the FIFTH, not the fourth; the series skips the MT 45:11 frame exactly as at the sibling row, and no counted domain is named. ADDRESSEE CONTRAST: byte-exact and the more serious. MT 45:18 is third- and first-person throughout -- its object suffixes are all feminine singular referring to the earth, לֹא תֹ֥הוּ בְרָאָ֖הּ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת יְצָרָ֑הּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.18), closing on a first-person self-declaration -- and MT 45:19 is first-person report whose only mention of Jacob's offspring is לֹ֥א אָמַ֛רְתִּי לְזֶ֥רַע יַעֲקֹ֖ב תֹּ֣הוּ בַקְּשׁ֑וּנִי (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.19), where the offspring stand as the indirect object of a NEGATED report and the plural imperative inside it sits within the quoted speech being denied. There is no vocative and no second-person verb or suffix anywhere in the row's span, so the row's device_notes sets MT 45:20's onset against an address that does not exist in its own span. The seam itself is not in doubt and I do not disturb it: MT 45:20 opens הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.20) -- three plural imperative forms followed by the addressed group -- which is sufficient tier-1 evidence standing alone. One precision on the challenge's wording: Hebrew marks no vocative, so 'plural vocative' is a construal resting on the three plural imperatives rather than a byte-marked form; the imperatives are the byte-visible part and should carry the claim. The rival is correctly credited: the exclusive-deity formula does straddle the seam, וְאֵ֥ין עֽוֹד at MT 45:18 (byte tier) recurring at MT 45:21 and MT 45:22 (sweep: 7 verses book-wide carry that skeleton, 6 of them in ch 45), and the row discloses the joined-speech reading. The frame's non-initial position is handled honestly -- the row splices the causal particle with the formula, כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.18), with the tetragrammaton immediately following, so the frame owner is the divine class. Marks: PE after MT 45:17 before the span, none inside (tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-016. (a) Field device_notes: delete the contrast with an 'address to the offspring of Jacob' and rest the seam on MT 45:20's own onset, spliced at byte tier as הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם -- three plural imperative forms followed by the named addressed group. If a contrast is wanted, use the byte-true one: this row's span carries no vocative and no second-person form at all, its offspring-of-Jacob phrase standing as the indirect object of a negated report at MT 45:19. (b) Field boundary_rationale: fix the ordinal in the SAME series-wide sweep as the sibling row -- name the counted object and range (messenger-formula onsets in MT 44:23-45:25, MT 45:18 being the fifth of five) or drop the ordinal. Test the cure must pass: every addressee or person contrast in the row must have BOTH of its terms present in the bytes of the verses it names -- the test that killed the original was that MT 45:18-45:19 carry no second-person form -- and every ordinal re-derives against a named, swept range.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's one recurrence claim -- that the summons takes up 'the same declare-and-witness vocabulary as the earlier trial speeches' -- carries no tier label, no digit, and no verse anchor, and the closing sentence grounds the row's rear edge in the work assignment rather than in the text.
rulings.grounds: Both defects verify and neither touches the bounds. (1) The recurrence claim names no verse, labels no tier and carries no digit, so it is evidence-free prose in a campaign where every recurrence is tier-labelled at write time and where no verse it argues can be mirrored in the evidence refs. The claim is checkable and true: the imperative pair is הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.21), and that imperative's skeleton stands in 6 verses book-wide, the trial-speech sites among them being MT 41:22 and MT 41:23 (verified) -- so the fix is purely additive, which is why low is the right band. (2) The closing phrase 'the end of the assigned range' argues the row's rear edge from the work unit rather than from the text, which the register law bars outright: work-unit and file-order talk never appears in row prose, and cross-row references are verse-anchored. The honest byte statement is available -- MT 46:1 opens a different subject with a burden-noun, נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.46.1), which belongs to the load-carry family and not to the verse-initial oracle headers, so the following verse begins no header-bounded oracle. Bounds stand and I do not disturb them: MT 45:20's plural imperatives plus named addressed group are tier-1 and byte-verified, and the closing verdict is בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.25). The mark report verifies exactly: no PE and no SAMEKH from MT 45:18 through MT 45:25, the layer's section running from the PE after MT 45:17 to the SAMEKH after MT 46:2. The challenge is right to present that grouping as running toward the row's disclosed rival AND right not to press it as a defect -- absence is never counterevidence and no mark stands adjacent to either seam -- so it stays out of the mandatory remedy. NEW FINDING, neither primary's: the row's own absence statement, that no marked-division disclosure applies within the span or at its front seam, is byte-checkable but carries no digit where the sanctioned shorthand would give one (0 marked verses in MT 45:20-45:25); a zero-count claim carries the same digit discipline as a positive one.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-017. (a) Field boundary_rationale: anchor the recurrence -- name the earlier trial-speech verses MT 41:22 and MT 41:23, splice the imperative pair הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ at byte tier at oshb:Isa.45.21, label the tier (skeleton, shared imperative form) and carry the digit (sweep: 6 verses book-wide) -- then mirror the newly argued out-of-span verses in boundary_evidence_refs. (b) Field boundary_rationale: delete 'and the end of the assigned range'; if a rear-edge statement is wanted, replace it with the byte statement that the next verse opens a different subject with a burden-noun that is not one of the verse-initial oracle headers. (c) Field device_notes: give the absence statement its digit under the sanctioned shorthand. Test the cure must pass: no work-unit, file-order or positional reference survives anywhere in row prose, every recurrence carries verse anchors, tier and digit, and every verse newly argued in prose appears in the evidence refs -- the tests that killed the original were an unanchored recurrence claim and a rear edge grounded in the work assignment.
